lessons.title: Perimeter and Area of 2D Shapes
lessons.concept: Mensuration deals with measuring lengths, areas, and volumes. For 2D shapes, perimeter is the total boundary length and area is the surface enclosed. Common shapes include rectangle, square, triangle, and circle.
lessons.formula: Rectangle: P = 2(l + w), A = l*w. Square: P = 4a, A = a^2. Triangle: A = (1/2)*b*h. Circle: C = 2*pi*r, A = pi*r^2.
lessons.worked_example: A rectangle has length 10 cm and width 4 cm. Perimeter = 2(10+4)=28 cm. Area = 10*4=40 cm^2.
mistakes: Using diameter in place of radius in circle formulas (or vice versa)
Forgetting to divide by 2 for triangle area
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Surface Area and Volume of 3D Solids
lessons.concept: 3D solids have surface area (total area of outer faces/surfaces) and volume (space occupied). Basic solids in aptitude include cube, cuboid, cylinder, and sphere.
lessons.formula: Cube (side a): TSA = 6a^2, V = a^3. Cuboid (l,w,h): TSA = 2(lw+lh+wh), V = l*w*h. Cylinder (r,h): CSA = 2*pi*r*h, TSA = 2*pi*r*(h+r), V = pi*r^2*h.
lessons.worked_example: Cube with side 3 cm: volume = 3^3 = 27 cm^3, total surface area = 6*3^2 = 54 cm^2.
mistakes: Confusing total surface area with curved/lateral surface area
Using wrong units (cm^2 for volume or cm^3 for area)
Substituting diameter directly as r in cylinder formulas

lessons.title: Units and Conversions in Mensuration
lessons.concept: Correct units are essential: lengths use cm/m, areas use cm^2/m^2, and volumes use cm^3/m^3. When converting units, square or cube the linear conversion factor for area and volume respectively.
mistakes: Converting area/volume using linear factor only (not squared/cubed)
Mixing units in the same calculation
Misplacing decimal point during metric conversion
